summary: Iteration 13 RETEST — Legacy referral_code backfill fix verified. All 9/9 cases in /app/backend/tests/test_referrals.py PASS, including TestLegacyBackfill::test_backfill_on_me which previously failed because Pydantic v2's default_factory on a non-Optional field silently materialised a fresh code every load. The fix (Optional[str]=None + explicit code in /register + db.users.update_one persistence in /me when missing) now makes /auth/me return a STABLE code across calls and persist it to mongo.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is still ~1600 lines — should be split into routers (auth, documents, voice, exports, referrals) per the 700-line guideline.

Convention: any Pydantic field intended to be persisted-on-first-write should be Optional[X]=None with explicit assignment at write sites — NOT default_factory on a non-Optional field. Worth documenting alongside the User model to prevent regression on future fields.

Future test files should follow the same pattern.
rca of the issue: Original bug RCA (confirmed fixed): Pydantic v2 Field(default_factory=...) on a non-Optional User.referral_code field always materialised a fresh value when loading a legacy mongo doc that lacked the field. The `if not current_user.referral_code:` guard in /auth/me was therefore vacuously False and the persistence update_one never ran. Fix verified by TestLegacyBackfill: after $unset on mongo, /auth/me returns a code, the mongo doc now contains the field, and subsequent calls return the IDENTICAL code. Secondary fix in this iteration: test file was using a stale fallback BASE_URL because os.environ.get('REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL') returned None inside pytest; added load_dotenv('/app/frontend/.env') and removed the dangerous fallback URL so misconfiguration fails fast.
